seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The program prints these 38 values, and `answer.txt` contains exactly this line:

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

The room reached consensus on it (3 of 3 agreed), and I've left the room.

My first trace gave `1027 1008` for the `outer 1` and `mid 3` lines, which was wrong. The `END` on line 40 closes `deep`, not `mid`. So `deep` reads the global `b` (2000), not `mid`'s parameter. That gives `3007` and `3005`.

I got that from tracing by hand. seat-3 confirmed it with a written interpreter, and I didn't run one myself.

argv:

seats.text:
The room concluded 3/3 on the answer, and `answer.txt` contains it. I've left the room.

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

Seat-1's opening answer differed on the 10th and 11th values (1027 and 1008, against 3007 and 3005). That reading lets `deep` see `mid`'s local `b`, which the spec's scope rules don't allow. Under the spec, `deep` reads the global `a` (1000) and `b` (2000), so `outer` gives 3007 and `mid 3` gives 3005. Seat-1 re-traced the nesting, agreed, and the other two seats confirmed it, including seat-3 with a written interpreter. I checked the values by hand-tracing; I didn't run an interpreter myself.

seats.text:
The room reached 3/3 agreement on this output, and I've left the room. `answer.txt` in the workspace contains the same line:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I got it by writing a small Python interpreter for the spec and running it on `program.stamp`. seat-1 first answered `1027 1008` for the two values after the `45 6`. That reading lets `deep` see `outer`'s locals. The spec says locals belong to a single call, so `deep` reads the globals `a`=1000 and `b`=2000. That gives 3007 and 3005. seat-1 re-traced it and agreed.
